name: What is the difference between ceramic, porcelain, and marble wall tiles?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between ceramic, porcelain, and marble wall tiles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ceramic and porcelain are engineered clay tiles that resist moisture and stains, whereas natural marble is porous stone requiring extra care. Ceramic is lightweight and easy to cut, making it great for backsplashes. Porcelain is denser and absorbs almost no water, making it ideal for high-moisture shower walls. Marble offers distinct, luxurious veining, but it is heavier, scratches more easily, and must be sealed before and after grouting to prevent discoloration. Choosing between them involves balancing the classic beauty of natural stone against the lower maintenance and durability of glazed porcelain.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ceramic and porcelain are durable, low-maintenance tiles ideal for moisture, while marble offers a unique natural look that requires routine sealing and careful care.
